question: Ritik and Sanjay together invested ₹77,600 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹19,000, Sanjay's share was ₹7,600. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ritik's profit = 19000 − 7600 = 11400.

Profit ratio (Ritik : Sanjay) = 11400 : 7600 = 3 : 2.

Investment ratio = Profit ratio (since the time period is identical) = 3 : 2.

Difference in investment parts = 3 − 2 = 1 part out of total 5 parts.

Difference in investment = 1/5 × 77600 = ₹15,520.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment of Ritik and Sanjay = ₹77,600

Total profit at the end of the year = ₹19,000

Sanjay's share in profit = ₹7,600

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Investment × Time

When the time period is constant, Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio

 Investment / Profit Ratio (Constant Time)
 
 Ritik
 
 3 Parts (₹11,400)
 
 Sanjay
 
 2 Parts (₹7,600)

 
 1 Part Diff

 
• 
 Total Investment = 5 Parts = ₹77,600

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ritik's profit = Total profit − Sanjay's profit

⇒ Ritik's profit = 19000 − 7600 = ₹11,400

⇒ Ratio of profits (Ritik : Sanjay) = 11400 : 7600 = 114 : 76 = 3 : 2

⇒ Since time is the same (1 year), investment ratio = profit ratio = 3 : 2

⇒ Let Ritik's investment be 3x and Sanjay's investment be 2x.

⇒ Total investment = 3x + 2x = 5x

⇒ 5x = 77600

⇒ x = 77600 ÷ 5 = ₹15,520

⇒ Difference in their investments = 3x − 2x = x

⇒ Difference = ₹15,520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner manages the business and usually receives a specific share or salary from the profit before the remaining profit is divided according to investment ratios. A sleeping partner only invests capital.

Different Investment Periods

When partners invest for different durations, their share in the profit is directly proportional to the product of their invested capital and the time period (Profit = Capital × Time).

Joining Mid-Way

If a new partner joins x months after the start of a financial year, their investment is calculated only for the remaining (12 − x) months of that year.
